cases.description: Generic 'all-in-one' copy scores low; wins concentrate in mid-market teams without RevOps, so positioning targets them against Clari/spreadsheets; rewrites use placeholders instead of invented proof.
cases.notes:
Homepage copy (current):
Headline: The all-in-one revenue platform.
Subhead: Our platform empowers revenue teams to unlock their full potential with AI-powered insights.
Supporting points: Real-time CRM sync. Explainable AI risk scoring. No-code rule builder. 15-minute setup.

Win/loss notes (last quarter):
- Won: mid-market sales org (120 reps), no RevOps team. Champion said: "Setup took one afternoon and the reps actually trust the score because it shows why."
- Won: mid-market SaaS (80 reps), no RevOps team, switched from spreadsheets. "We couldn't run Clari without an admin."
- Lost: enterprise (600 reps) with a 5-person RevOps team, chose Clari for breadth of forecasting features.
- Lost: enterprise (450 reps), chose Clari; "your tool is too light for our process."
- 40% of reps ignored the previous black-box tool's score because they couldn't see the reasoning.

Competitors and alternatives: Clari, spreadsheets, doing nothing.

assertions.why: every win is mid-market without RevOps; every loss is enterprise
not 'strong' (17+): the specific supporting points can't rescue an abstract headline and subhead
missing proof shown as a bracketed placeholder
the generic headline is called out under What's not landing
no unsupported generalizations or invented speakers
